BiblicalUsage: The word names a tenth, the tithe, and it runs from Abram to Malachi. Abram gave tithes of all to Melchizedek, priest of the most high God, and the law says all the tithe of the land is holy unto the LORD. Israel was to eat the tithe before the LORD in the place He chose, that they might learn to fear Him always, and Malachi says to bring all the tithes into the storehouse, that there may be meat in God's house.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the tithe teaches us that the first tenth belongs to God, and giving it is how we learn to fear Him and trust Him. I hold that God opens the windows of heaven to the cheerful giver, and the tithe is not a tax but a confession that everything we have is His.
